questions.note: Hallux longest and toes 3–5 descend, but toe 2 ends about 12 mm behind the hallux (spec 3–5) and the 5th points straight ahead beside the 4th instead of rotated and tucked under it. Knuckles exist, but as beads on waisted, straight, finger-like shafts with small pulps; plantar creases are raised rings; toes 3 and 4 are near copies; deep clefts split toes 3–5 apart.

Order and heights are right: the medial malleolus sits about 13 mm above the lateral (V8), the lateral is further back (plan, V4), and an Achilles ridge with shallow grooves either side reads in V8 and V3. But the medial malleolus barely breaks the inner contour (V8, V1f), the lateral is a broad soft mound rather than a pointed knob (V3), and there is no anterior ankle crease.

defects.what: Toe 2 ends about 12 mm behind the hallux tip in plan (about 75 px at 6.2 px/mm; V4o agrees), against the spec's 3–5 mm, so the toe line steps back steeply from a dominant big toe.
defects.fix: Lengthen toe 2 by about 7–9 mm through its middle and distal phalanges so its tip sits 3–5 mm behind the hallux, then re-grade toes 3–5 from it.

defects.what: Toes 2–5 stand apart with see-through gaps along their free length, and the 3–4 and 4–5 clefts reach about 65 and 78 mm behind the hallux tip (spec §3.2: about 51 and 59), so toes 3–5 read as long separate fingers.
defects.fix: Bring the 3–4 and 4–5 commissures forward so the web line curves gently with the metatarsal heads, and close the lesser toes up side by side, touching along their middle and distal phalanges as a booted foot's do.

defects.what: The 5th toe points straight ahead beside the 4th, nail up, with a clear gap between them; it is neither rotated 30–45° nor tucked under the 4th, so the toe row ends in a full upright toe.
defects.fix: Rotate the 5th toe into varus so its nail faces out and up, flex it slightly and nestle its pulp under the lateral side of the 4th toe.

defects.what: Toes 2–4 are slender, straight and finger-like: waisted proximal segments, bead-like PIP knuckles (toe 2's bulges sideways), pulps no wider than the shafts; toes 3 and 4 are near copies, and none flexes to press its pulp to the floor.
defects.fix: Real lesser toes are short and fleshy: the proximal segment as full as the joint, the PIP slightly raised, the distal segment angled down so a broad pulp spreads on the floor, each toe distinct in width and tilt.

defects.what: From behind the heel is a rounded box: near-vertical side walls from the floor to about 50 mm, a broad flat back face and a square shoulder under the lateral malleolus, as wide at its top as at the floor.
defects.fix: A real heel narrows upward from the spread pad to the ~25 mm tuberosity under the Achilles, with a smooth hollow under each malleolus, so from behind it reads as a rounded bulb, not a block.

defects.what: The medial malleolus barely swells the inner contour (about 2–3 mm against about 11 mm for the lateral) and does not break the medial contour in V1f either, so the ankle reads one-sided.
defects.fix: Build it as a broad round bony dome about 30 mm across and 5 mm proud of the shin line, higher and further forward than the lateral malleolus.

defects.what: The lateral malleolus is a broad soft mound about 40 mm tall that fades into the heel, not the narrower pointed bony knob whose lower tip stands clear above the hollow behind and below it.
defects.fix: Narrow it to a ~24 mm dome with a defined, downward-pointing tip and firm edges where bone lies under thin skin, with the peroneal groove behind and below it.

defects.what: No anterior ankle crease: the front of the ankle sweeps smoothly from the shin into the dorsum with no dorsiflexion fold at about 80–84 mm height (none in V3 either).
defects.fix: Add one horizontal fold across the front of the ankle, bowed slightly toward the toes, with two or three fainter parallel lines above it.

defects.what: A hairline vertical seam about 15 mm long runs down the skin below the medial malleolus, a mesh crease no real ankle has.
defects.fix: Remove the crease so the skin below the malleolus is continuous.

defects.what: An isolated round dimple about 14 × 7 mm sits on the medial midfoot about 25 mm above the floor, reading as a dent rather than part of the arch.
defects.fix: Let the medial arch be one long smooth vault from heel pad to ball, the abductor hallucis full above its plantar edge, with no local pit.

defects.what: From below toes 2–5 are thin tubes wrapped in raised parallel rings with small knob pulps, like banded sausages, separated by gaps; real toes show round fleshy pads split by a few deep creases.
defects.fix: Give each lesser toe's sole two or three fat pads with creases cut between them at the joints and a broad round pulp at the tip, the toes packed together.

defects.what: The first metatarsal head is a separate round knob with pinched contours above and below it, like a small bunion, rather than a broad medial swell running smoothly into the hallux.
defects.fix: Blend the head into a broad convex medial border (radius about 14 mm) continuous with the hallux and the shaft.

defects.what: The 5th metatarsal styloid shows as a small isolated bead on the lateral border, like a pea under the skin.
defects.fix: Make it a ridge-like prominence that rises out of the lateral border and fades forward along the shaft.

defects.what: A small pinched Y-shaped fold sits on the sole under the lateral midfoot near the styloid, a crease no unloaded sole has there.
defects.fix: Smooth the sole there into the continuous surface of the lateral band.

defects.what: From below the ball is not a separate transverse cushion: the sole runs smooth into the toe webs with no sulcus, so the toes look attached to a paddle instead of rising from behind a pad.
defects.fix: Real soles show the metatarsal pad as a broad oblique cushion that ends in a deep crease at the toe bases.

defects.what: In profile the back of the heel ramps straight up into the Achilles: the contour slopes back about 10 mm from 100 down to 52 mm height with no concave notch above the calcaneal tuberosity, so the heel reads soft and swollen.
defects.fix: Let the Achilles come down nearly vertical to its insertion at about 52 mm, then turn through a short concave fillet into the convex tuberosity.

ranked: [D2] The lesser toes are split apart: gaps run the length of toes 2–5 and the 3–4 and 4–5 clefts reach deep into the ball, so the forefoot reads as separate fingers and looks long in plan. A booted man's toes lie packed and webbed, the hallux leaning in toward toe 2.
[D1] Toe 2 stops about 12 mm short of the hallux (spec 3–5 mm), so the toe line drops steeply from an oversized-looking big toe and the forefoot looks lopsided toward the medial side in plan.

[D4] Toes 2–4 are long, straight and slender with waisted shafts and bead knuckles, like fingers; real toes are short and fleshy, the knuckle a little raised and the tip angled down onto a broad pulp. Toes 3 and 4 are near copies.
[D3] The 5th toe stands straight and upright beside the 4th with a gap, nail up; an adult's 5th toe is rotated outward, curled and tucked against or under the 4th.

[D5] From behind the heel is a rounded box with vertical walls and a square shoulder under the lateral malleolus; a real heel tapers upward from the pad into the Achilles insertion like a bulb, with soft hollows under both malleoli.

[D6] The medial malleolus hardly shows (V8, V1f), so the ankle reads one-sided with only the lateral bump; a real medial malleolus is a broad round bony dome, about as prominent as the lateral, higher and further forward.
[D11] From below the lesser toes look like banded sausages: thin tubes with raised parallel rings and knob tips, instead of round fleshy pads split by a few deep creases.
[D15] The sole has no distinct ball cushion or toe-base crease; it runs smooth from the arch into the webs, so the plantar view reads as a mannequin paddle with toes attached.
[D7] The lateral malleolus is a broad soft mound fading into the heel; on a lean man it is a narrower, pointed bony knob whose tip stands clear above the hollow beneath it.
[D16] In profile the back of the heel ramps straight up into the Achilles with no concave notch above the tuberosity, so the heel looks soft and swollen rather than bony.
[D8] No anterior ankle crease: the front of the ankle is one smooth sweep from shin to dorsum, where a real ankle shows a fold at the talar neck with fainter lines above it.
[D12] The first metatarsal head is a separate round knob with pinched contours above and below, reading as a small bunion rather than a broad medial swell flowing into the hallux.
[D10] A small round dimple on the medial midfoot (V2) reads as a dent; the real arch is one long smooth vault with the abductor hallucis full above its plantar edge.
[D13] The 5th metatarsal styloid is a small isolated bead on the lateral border (V1f), like a pea under the skin, rather than a ridge rising out of the border.
[D9] A hairline vertical seam about 15 mm long runs down the skin under the medial malleolus (V2).
[D14] A small pinched Y-shaped fold sits on the sole under the lateral midfoot (V4).

The declared vein relief is heavy enough to hide the dorsum's large form in V1f, V5f and the plan: the piped network cuts the instep into strips, so its transverse doming can be judged only in profile.
